samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` is worst-case quadratic in the merge count and runs synchronously inside `doc.update` on every `PUT .../freeze` and every `POST .../insert|delete`, giving an authenticated write-scoped caller a single-request event-loop DoS of the whole backend process.
samples.evidence: Attack: (1) `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/tabs/:t/merges` with a chain of small merges whose JSON key order is *descending* — `{"A50000":{"rs":2,"cs":1}, "A49999":{...}, ... "A1":{...}}`. `parseMerges` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:107) validates each key/span but caps neither the number of entries nor their arrangement, and the global body limit is 25MB (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20), so ~50k–1M entries fit. (2) `PUT .../freeze {rows:1}` → worksheet.controller.ts:112 calls `snapFreezePastMerges`. The inner `for` (merging.ts:219) walks every entry doing a `parseRef` + object allocs; because the straddling block that advances `rows` is always the *last* entry visited, each outer `while` pass advances the boundary by exactly one and `changed` stays true, so the loop runs O(n) passes × O(n) entries. At n=50k that is ~2.5e9 `parseRef` calls (minutes of blocked CPU); at n=1e6 it is ~1e12 (effectively a hang). This runs inside a synchronous `doc.update` callback on an attached Yorkie document in Node's single-threaded event loop, so every other tenant's request on that process stalls for the duration. The same code path is re-entered from `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278) on every insert/delete, and from `Sheet.shiftCells`/`setFreezePane` in the browser, so a collaborator can also hang victims' editor tabs. Before this change neither `PUT freeze` nor the shift path iterated the merge map repeatedly, so the quadratic factor is new.

samples.summary: `parseMerges` bounds each individual span but places no cap on the *number* of merge entries, which is what makes the new repeated-scan freeze snap (and the pre-existing per-load `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walk) attacker-amplifiable.
samples.evidence: `parseMerges` validates key round-trip, grid bounds and `rs*cs <= MaxMergedCells` per entry, but the loop at worksheet-settings.ts:121 accepts an unbounded entry count; with the 25MB body limit (main.ts:20) that is ~1M merges. Every consumer added by this change iterates that map — `snapFreezePastMerges` repeatedly (merging.ts:217), `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` once per move (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:192) — and `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:851) walks `rs*cs` per entry on every document load, so the same body also makes the tab expensive-to-open for every collaborator. A `MaxMerges` count cap alongside `MaxMergedCells` would remove the amplifier the new snap depends on.
searchedFor: grep snapFreezePastMerges|crossesFreezePane repo-wide for all call sites

samples.summary: `PUT .../freeze` now stores a freeze value *derived* from stored merge spans instead of the validated request value, so a merge written by a non-API writer (xlsx import, direct Yorkie client) can push `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` past the grid bound `parseFreeze` exists to enforce.
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` clamps rows/cols to 1,000,000 / 18,278 precisely because (its own comment, worksheet-settings.ts:47-53) an out-of-grid freeze makes the frozen quadrants allocate per frame so the UI never paints and the user can no longer reach the freeze menu to undo it. Line 117 now assigns `snapped.frozenRows`, which is `range[1].r` of whatever merge straddles the boundary (merging.ts:222) — a number never re-validated. Merge spans reaching the document from outside this validator are not clamped: `applyMergeRanges` in packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts:252 computes `rowSpan` straight from an attacker-supplied `mergeCell ref` with no grid bound, and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:969 writes merges into the CRDT directly. So: import a crafted .xlsx containing `<mergeCell ref="A1:A9999999"/>`, then call `PUT freeze {rows:1}` → the tab is persisted with a freeze far outside the grid, the exact unrecoverable state the bound was written to prevent. Same derived-write bypass exists in `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:284) on insert/delete. Fix: clamp the snapped result to the same MaxRows/MaxColumns bounds before storing.

samples.summary: `PUT .../freeze` now parses every stored merge key, so a single unparsable merge key in the document turns a previously merge-independent endpoint into a permanent 500.
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` calls `parseRef(anchorSref)` unguarded (merging.ts:220) and `parseRef` throws `Invalid Reference` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:351). Merge keys are only round-trip-validated on the `PUT merges` path; a key written straight into the CRDT by a client (yorkie-store.ts:969) or carried in by an import is not. Before this change `setFreeze` touched only `frozenRows`/`frozenCols`, so it was a recovery path that still worked on such a document; now the throw escapes `doc.update` and the handler answers 500 for that tab indefinitely, removing the way to fix the document through the API. Wrapping the parse (or skipping unparsable keys) keeps the endpoint available.

samples.summary: Removing the post-paste `clearCopyBuffer()` makes the in-memory snapshot of copied cell content (values, formulas, styles) live for the whole editor session rather than until the next paste.
samples.evidence: Both view paste paths (view/worksheet.ts and view/spreadsheet.ts:724) no longer call `sheet.clearCopyBuffer()`, and `Sheet.copyBuffer` retains the full copied grid; only Escape or a consumed cut drops it. Copied cells may hold sensitive data, and it now persists in the tab's heap indefinitely (and is reachable from any later paste). Deliberate and justified in the change for repeat-paste behaviour; noted only as a data-retention hardening consideration, not an exploitable flaw.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out in the repo. merging.ts:217-230 is a restart-on-change full rescan with a per-entry parseRef/allocation and no iteration bound; an overlapping chain of 2-row merges supplied in descending key order advances the boundary one row per O(n) pass, giving O(n^2). parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) bounds each key, span, and per-merge cell count but caps neither the number of entries nor overlap, and main.ts:20 allows a 25MB JSON body (~1e6 entries). The setup is not blocked by assertMergesClearOfFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:189 returns early when both freeze counts are 0), so the attacker stores the chain with freeze=0 and then hits PUT freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:112-116), which runs snapFreezePastMerges synchronously inside doc.update; the same function is re-entered on insert/delete via worksheet-structure.ts:278. safeWorksheetRecordEntries is a plain Object.entries (worksheet-record.ts:47-61), so the adversarial ordering is preserved. Only auth/scope guards protect the route (worksheet.controller.ts:51-52), so an authenticated write-scoped caller blocks the single-threaded event loop for the whole backend process with one request. Unbounded-input algorithmic resource exhaustion is within the security lens (unsafe input handling / availability), and I found no guard, cap, or normalization that makes it unreachable.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) bounds each entry (key round-trip :130, grid bounds :135, rs*cs <= MaxMergedCells :148 with MaxMergedCells=100000 at :23) but the Object.entries loop at :121 has no cap on the number of entries and no total-cells accumulator. No count cap exists anywhere else on this path: the only entry-count constant in the backend is MaxAxisEntries=10000 (worksheet-structure.ts:56, enforced :205/:226) which governs row/column insert/move counts, not merges; the route takes `@Body() body: unknown` with no DTO/ArrayMaxSize/interceptor (worksheet.controller.ts:231-234); stores return the map wholesale (sheets/src/store/memory.ts:594-596). The only byte bound is JSON_BODY_LIMIT='25mb' (main.ts:20, applied :49-50), which permits roughly a million ~20-byte entries, each free to declare up to 100k covered cells — so it does not bound the amplified work. Consumers iterate unbounded: snapFreezePastMerges re-scans all entries in a while(changed) loop (sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:212-230) from PUT freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:112-116), assertMergesClearOfFreeze iterates per PUT (worksheet.controller.ts:190-199), and Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap inserts one Map entry per covered cell (sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:851-853) on every load via loadMerges (sheet.ts:577-579), so the stored body makes the tab expensive/impossible to open for every collaborator. Vector: an authenticated user with workspace write scope (guards at worksheet.controller.ts:52) PUTs a merges map with ~1M distinct anchors each rs*cs near 100000; the request is accepted, persisted, and every later load rebuilds a cover map of ~1e11 entries. Resource exhaustion / availability (CWE-770) rather than authz or injection, so it sits at the edge of this lens's enumerated lanes, but it is a real, unguarded, attacker-controlled amplifier and I found no counterexample to refute the absence claim.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described — worksheet.controller.ts:117-119 stores snapped.frozenRows/Cols derived from merges, snapFreezePastMerges (merging.ts:221-228) never re-clamps, and xlsx-importer.ts:247-262 builds merge spans from an attacker-supplied `ref` with no grid bound. But it is not a Security-lens blocking defect. (1) No trust boundary is crossed: the endpoint is behind CombinedAuthGuard/WorkspaceScopeGuard/ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard (worksheet.controller.ts:52) and the precondition (an out-of-grid merge already in the document) requires equal-or-greater write capability. (2) The validator is not bypassable through the API surface itself: parseMerges caps rs/cs to the grid plus a 100k-cell ceiling (worksheet-settings.ts:135-152), so no API-created merge can push the snap past MaxRows/MaxColumns. (3) The controller mirrors, rather than weakens, existing behaviour: Sheet.setFreezePane performs the identical unclamped snap (sheet.ts:532-551) and yorkie-store.ts:1146-1160 persists it verbatim, so the same state is reachable through the editor with no API call. (4) Impact is client-side render cost only — no backend code iterates frozenRows (grep across packages/backend/src shows only copy/migration and this controller) — and by the repo's own MaxMergedCells rationale (worksheet-settings.ts:13-23) the prerequisite giant merge is itself the unopenable-document condition, so clamping line 117 would not remove the harmful state. That makes this an unbounded-value/robustness hardening item for the correctness lens, not authorization, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF, or deserialization.

finding.summary: `parseMerges` caps the cells per merge but not the number of merge entries, leaving the merge map an unbounded attacker-controlled input to every merge-walking code path (now including insert/delete)
finding.evidence: `parseMerges` validates each key and caps `rs*cs` at `MaxMergedCells = 100000` (line 148) precisely because `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walks span area; no equivalent cap exists on `Object.entries(merges).length`, so a single 25MB `PUT merges` body can store hundreds of thousands of entries. Every merge walk then scales with that: `assertMoveKeepsMerges`/`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:154,192), `assertMergesClearOfFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:190), and now `snapFreezePastMerges` on every insert/delete (worksheet-structure.ts:278), the last of which is superlinear. Attacker cost is one request; server cost is unbounded CPU inside a synchronous `doc.update`.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) bounds each key and caps rs*cs at MaxMergedCells (line 148/23) but never checks Object.entries(merges).length; the loop copies every entry through. The only ceiling on entry count is the 25MB body-parser limit (main.ts:20,49-50), which allows on the order of a million ~20-byte entries in one request. I grepped repo-wide for cap constants (const Max…/MAX_… in packages/backend/src — the codebase does cap counts elsewhere, e.g. MaxAxisEntries=10000 at yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:56, but nothing for merges), read every backend file containing "merges" (16 files), checked the PUT merges handler (worksheet.controller.ts:226-255, @Body() body: unknown so ValidationPipe does not apply), the class guards (worksheet.controller.ts:51-52, authz only), and the global throttler (app.module.ts:97-102, 120/min — no per-route tightening). No entry-count bound exists anywhere on this path. The consumers named in the finding check out: assertMergesClearOfFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:190), assertMoveKeepsMerges (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:154), assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze (:192-194), and snapFreezePastMerges reached on every insert/delete via applyWorksheetShift (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278). snapFreezePastMerges (merging.ts:207-233) is a while(changed) loop over all entries whose doc comment argues termination but not a bound; since each pass advances the boundary by at most one block and plain-object key order is insertion order (so attacker-ordered), a chained merge map makes it O(n^2). All of it runs synchronously inside doc.update with no timeout, so one authenticated request blocks the Node event loop for the whole process, not just the attacker's own document — attacker-controlled unbounded resource consumption (CWE-770), an availability weakness rather than a mere correctness bug. I could not find a counterexample cap, so the finding stands.
